Q7 (drafter D): four points.
(1) The matrix agent value for Grok rows and so the matrixAdapters key (the spec assumes "grok", case-insensitive, written "--agent Grok" in the reported commands).
(2) How write roles run on grok: tool names with a permission mode ("--tools", "--permission-mode"; "--tools" takes names, not the claude-style patterns in Request.Allowlist) or a sandbox profile as codex does (decision 100, vendor.codex-write); the six probes only measure the first and not a full write path, so the spec makes the implementer stop and report if probes 04 and 05 do not show a safe mode. Drafter recommendation: decide after the probes, with their output in hand; do not allow bypassPermissions.
(3) Slot cap for grok: none (defaultVendorCaps unchanged). Drafter recommendation: none until a limit is seen.
(4) Doctor login line: none unless a probe finds a reliable no-cost command ("grok models" said "not authenticated" while "-p" worked); the spec adds nothing otherwise.

items.title: Engine follows relay v11 process rules: gate close timing and [AFTER LAND] Check lines
items.short_title: Engine v11 process rules

note_records.text: **2026-10-30** — From S198 review (2026-10-30): a v11 gate step is closed with the report's verdict at internal/engine/round.go:400, before a TriageGate shape error (round.go:471-481) or an Owner needed question (round.go:493-505) can pause the round, so the ledger can show pass for a round the engine did not accept; a retry then records a second gate round that slicer's gate_rounds/with_verdict counts (../slicer/src/slicer/relayrun.py:973-982) would count twice (retry behaviour not traced). Decide whether such a round closes with its verdict (now) or without one.

**2026-11-01** — Open owner questions from the 2026-10-31 spec drafting. Ask the owner before the relay starts; the spec waits on these.

Q1 (drafter C; suggested adj key relay.gate-verdict): does a v11 gate round close with its verdict before the engine accepts the round?
What the drafter traced: internal/engine/round.go:439-462: for a v11 gate the step is closed with "--phase done --verdict pass or fail" right after the report is read, before TriageGate (:477), before the "## Owner needed" pause (:500-509) and before the [owner blocker] hold (:513-530). CheckReport returns no report on a shape error, so a report with a bad first line already closes without a verdict (TestV11GateWithoutAVerdictLineClosesWithoutOne). After a pause, Answer or Retry runs the gate again as a new attempt with a new ledger step (round.go:226-233 names the attempt, stepStart at :605-622 opens the step), and the engine counts the slice's gate FAILs only for accepted rounds (internal/engine/states.go:554-584, rec.Fails++). slicer's _measure counts every gate-role lane step as a gate round regardless of phase and verdict (../slicer/src/slicer/relayrun.py:973-982), so the retried gate is two gate rounds in both options. What the verdict changes: with the verdict on the first step, with_verdict counts it and gate_fails counts it when it says fail although ork wrote no "Review FAIL" note and did not send the slice back; without it, gates.by_proxy counts the round (:1052) and gate_fails counts it only when an implementer fix round follows it (:977-982), which a retried gate is not. So the "twice" in the S198 note is two rounds, not one verdict counted twice; the real difference is a verdict in the ledger for a round ork did not act on.
Options: (a) keep: close with the verdict as the report says it; the ledger shows a PASS or FAIL for a round that then paused. (b) Close with the verdict only for a round the engine accepts (the one that returns outcome ok true, round.go:534); a round paused for a shape error, an owner question or a blocker finding closes done with no verdict, and the retried gate carries it. (c) Close such a round "--phase fail --reason ..." with no verdict; the drafter does not recommend it: fail means the role's process failed, and the run tree draws it as a failed step.
Drafter recommendation: (b): the ledger verdict matches what ork acted on.
Waits: S204 Implement step 3 and the "Gate close" tests. Other S204 steps do not wait.

Q2 (drafter C): how are v11 rules 1 and 2 recorded?
Rule 1, "a small fix round is checked and gated in one pass by the read-only role that raised its findings": ork's fix round goes to checks and then the gate, which resumes the reviewer's session (internal/engine/states.go:164-176,523-531); there is no second review round. Pinned by TestReviewFindingsStartAFixRoundAndTheResumedReviewerGatesIt (internal/engine/engine_test.go:361).
Rule 2, "a clean merge of main is regated by the one-pass small-fix check on the merge diff": ork merges main in, renders, re-runs the project check command and "slicer check", then fast-forwards, with no role round (internal/engine/land.go:110-175); the ledger run has already ended at the finish step, so a regate round could not be recorded (S153).
Options: (a) document rule 1 as met and rule 2 as a deviation in docs/design.md and docs/orchestrator-parity.md; (b) build a one-pass gate round on the merge diff in land.go with no ledger step: a separate M, E-class slice.
Drafter recommendation: (a): nothing to build, and it matches how ork already runs.
Waits: the wording of two docs rows in S204 step 7; no code.

Q3 (drafter C): does ork run an [AFTER LAND] Check line itself at landing?
Options: (a) no: the approval card lists each such line as "deferred to land: ..." (already in state later), and the owner runs it after landing; ork runs only the project check command, never a slice's Check lines, and a line may be prose. (b) Yes, for a line that is one backticked command: run it in the main checkout after the fast-forward, and a failure pauses the slice. A separate slice.
Drafter recommendation: (a).
Waits: S204 Implement step 4 is written for (a); under (b) report and stop.

**2026-11-10** — Human checks at approval (S204):
- later: [AFTER LAND] After this lands, on a scratch project with slicer v1.17 installed, one relay whose slice has a `[AFTER LAND]` Check line reaches approval with that line shown as "deferred to land" and approves without a tick.

**2026-11-10** — Verified: a v11 gate round closes its ledger step with the verdict only when the engine accepts the round (closeStep in internal/engine/round.go); a round paused for a shape problem, an owner question or a blocker finding closes without one and the rerun is a new step. A Check line marked [AFTER LAND], with or without [HUMAN CHECK], shows on the approval card as 'deferred to land: ...' already in state later (owner marks kept); the implementer and gate prompts say not to run it. **2026-11-01** — Open owner questions from the 2026-10-31 spec drafting. Ask the owner before the relay starts; the spec waits on these.

NW-Q1 (drafter E): how do define, list, rm and start name the project, and does "start NAME" take it from the saved wave? The brief's forms have no project, but the file is keyed by project and name and "wave start" takes PROJECT ITEM... today (internal/cli/wave.go:100-102).
Options: (a) a "--project P" flag: required on define, optional on list, optional on rm and start when the name is unique across projects (the saved wave supplies the project), required when ambiguous; (b) positional "ork wave define P NAME ITEM..." and "ork wave start P NAME" (but "start P NAME" is indistinguishable from "start P ITEM"); (c) "--project" always required.
Drafter recommendation: (a): one positional means a name, two or more keep the typed form, nothing existing changes.
Waits: the CLI step and TestWaveProjectArgumentFollowsNWQ1.

NW-Q2 (drafter E): name syntax and limits.
Options: (a) 1 to 32 characters of [a-z0-9._-], starting with a letter or digit, never starting with "wave-" (adj 138 tells wave ids from run ids by that prefix), case-sensitive; item ids must exist as written, no repeats, at most 20 items; (b) any single-line text up to 64 characters without NUL, any number of items.
Drafter recommendation: (a).
Waits: wavestore name rules and tests.

NW-Q3 (drafter E): what does define do with a name that already exists for the project?
Options: (a) refuse with duplicate_name unless "--replace" is given (the TUI asks "Replace NAME? [y/N]"); (b) replace silently; (c) always refuse (remove first).
Drafter recommendation: (a).
Waits: TestWaveDefineDuplicateNameFollowsNWQ3 and the TUI replace test.

NW-Q4 (drafter E): unknown, retired or done members. At define time: (a) refuse an item slicer does not know (recommended); (b) accept it. At start time, for a member that is done (already decided: skipped), retired, or no longer in slicer: (a) skip it like a done member and name it with its status, never rewriting the saved file (recommended); (b) refuse the whole start naming them; (c) drop them from the saved wave.
Waits: Startable, TestWaveDefineItemRulesFollowNWQ4, TestSavedWaveStartableSkipsDoneRetiredAndMissing.

NW-Q5 (drafter E): file name, directory and mode. The brief says next to the registry.
Options: file waves.json in the registry's directory (~/.config/ork/, found as filepath.Dir of the registry path so tests need no new setting) with mode 0644 like projects.json, or 0600 (it holds only names and item ids); or ~/.local/state/ork/waves.json beside the run records.
Drafter recommendation: waves.json beside projects.json, mode 0600 (no cost, least exposure).
Waits: wavestore, docs/state.md, the mode test.

NW-Q6 (drafter E): "ork projects rm" and saved waves of that project.
Options: (a) drop them in the same step, as spec-check state is dropped today (removeProjectSpecsLocked, internal/daemon/handlers.go:479-508); (b) keep them and list them as "project not registered"; (c) refuse while any exist.
Drafter recommendation: (a).
Waits: TestRemoveProjectKeepsOrDropsSavedWavesPerNWQ6.

Options: (a) not in the TUI for now (it is in "ork status --json"); (b) a "wave NAME" line in the run pane, which needs source.EngineRun and engineRuns changes and makes the TUI slice E-class. Drafter recommendation: (a).

**2026-11-01** — Open owner questions from the 2026-10-31 spec drafting. Ask the owner before the relay starts; the spec waits on these. The spec contains recommended answers for all three.

LM-Q1 (drafter E): where is the check computed?
Options: (a) a new read method run.landcheck that the TUI calls when the pane of an awaiting-approval run opens and on each refresh of that run (recommended: engineRuns runs under runs.mu and must not spawn git); (b) inside engineRuns for every snapshot (git under the run-manager lock; no); (c) once, when the card is built, stored in the card (stale by the time the owner approves).
Waits: daemon, Live, TUI refresh test.

**2026-11-04** — Owner 2026-11-04 evidence: the s443 landing in slicer paused with "Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: .slicer/index.json, log.jsonl, render/ROADMAP.*" because slicer main held uncommitted tracking edits (matrix rows, filings). It cost one approval round and a commit by the owner. The abort is the F40 case; warn before the landing starts (S217) or commit the tracking-only edits.

**2026-11-04** — Owner 2026-11-04 evidence (prism-ui wave): the ff-only merge was blocked twice because ork's own run-state writes left the main checkout's tracking files (.slicer/index.json, log.jsonl, render/*, a slice JSON) uncommitted; the orchestrator committed the project's .slicer in main and ran ork retry. The project is a subdirectory (libraries/prism-ui, tracking at libraries/prism-ui/.slicer) of a larger repo that also holds another ork project (libraries/prism) landing into the same branch. The S254 spec does not handle this as written: dirtyOverlap takes paths from changedPaths (git status --porcelain=v1, internal/engine/filescope.go:36) and git diff --name-only, both relative to the repo root, while the tracking set is matched as .slicer/; so libraries/prism-ui/.slicer/... takes the stop path, and git -C P add -A -- PATHS with root-relative paths from a subdirectory P would name the wrong files. The spec should match tracking paths under the project prefix (git rev-parse --show-prefix; S292 adds such a helper) and say that a sibling project's dirty .slicer is not this landing's to commit.

**2026-11-05** — Owner 2026-11-05 evidence (prism-ui wave, filed from S293's friction set): the ff-only landing paused on 'Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge' with only tracking files dirty (.slicer/log.jsonl, render/slices/ID.md) for U38, U37, U30 and U36; each time the fix was git add of the project's .slicer plus a 'slicer: run state' commit on main, then ork retry (platforms repo: dd7a66b, 21536a1, c193ecf, 44c3b56, e6196af on 2026-11-05). The owner asked for ork to commit these itself. This slice's answered design (Q1 b, commit by pathspec before the merge-in) already covers it, so no new slice was filed. Points to keep when it is built: match tracking paths under the project prefix (the 2026-11-04 note; prism-ui is libraries/prism-ui in its repo); a fixed message; never commit any path outside the project's tracking set, and a sibling project's .slicer is not this landing's. The owner's request also said 'only when nothing else is dirty'; Q3 as answered acts when the slice also changes the file and stops early for other overlapping dirty files, which is compatible but not identical; confirm with the owner when the slice is picked up.

**2026-11-08** — Landed. Later: limit the ID done sweep (land.go:89-102) to handoff mode and the paths slicer land wrote; landing lock is per project path, so sibling projects in one repo can overlap (S217 reuses dirtyOverlap).

items.title: S235 later notes: guard the watchdog against a sleep detector never started, and test that the daemon starts it
items.short_title: S235 later notes: guard the watchdog against a sleep detector never started, and test that the daemon starts it

note_records.text: **2026-11-09** — Verified: a Wake counts no sleep until Start has run (adj 199), and Start resets the sample time so an earlier jump is not counted. Wake.Started() is a read-only, nil-safe accessor (adj 200). TestUnstartedWakeDoesNotHideAHang failed first (the silent role was never killed) and now passes. TestRecoverRunsStartsTheWake fails when the Start call in recoverRuns is deleted. Every new assertion was mutation-checked. go test ./... (23 packages), go test -race ./internal/engine ./internal/daemon, go vet, gofmt, slicer check and adj lint are green. The human check of a real sleep over 35 minutes is still open.

fields.findings: From the S235 review and gate (2026-11-03), both later: (1) The daemon builds its sleep detector (Wake) once and starts it in recoverRuns. If the start is ever missed, only the watchdog's 30s tick samples the clock (internal/engine/watchdog.go:27). That equals the 30s sleep threshold (internal/engine/wake.go:25), so a tick that arrives slightly late counts 25s as sleep and a silent role could take hours to be killed. PLAUSIBLE: traced by reading, not run. Production starts it today (internal/daemon/runs.go:210). Fix: give the threshold a margin over the tick, for example 2 minutes, or count sleep only after Start has run. (2) No test fails if the Wake Start call at internal/daemon/runs.go:210 is removed; TestStatusCarriesWorkingForARunningRun checks only that both projects share one detector (internal/daemon/runs_test.go:2466). Human checks marked later at approval: a real 35+ minute sleep during a run (no hung pause, status shows slept), and the working line at 100 columns on a live run.

items.title: Spec check: a report-shape failure or a denied read command retries the same session once instead of failing
items.short_title: Spec check: a report-shape failure or a denied read command retries the same session once instead of failing

note_records.text: **2026-11-08** — Reverses the S143 rule that spec-check denials are never retried: the row asks for it, and no decided adj record forbids it (adj 93, 156, 158, 164 reviewed). A spec-check round that ends with a report-shape error or a denied command now resumes its own session once; an unclassified exit still stops (adj 23); vendor limits are not resumed. Later: re-check whether S277/S280 made spec-check denials rarer and say so here; after a resume the failure text no longer contains the word retry (daemon test covers only the no-session path); a first-round denial with no session no longer starts with spec-check exited CLASS; the spec check missed a deleted Failing tests section on all three local launchers (see .scratch/local-eval/report.md), so it is not reliable alone.

fields.findings: 2026-11-03: the spec check (claude sonnet high, row r16) failed on report shape twice on S72's first and third launches: 'spec check failed on its automatic retry; check again: report shape: S72: write Ready, or question blocks that start with Question:'. The third and fourth launches passed, so the failure is flaky. S243 gives every report-checked role one automatic nudge to the same session but says the spec check keeps its own retry (S243 Why, line 33), so the flake is not covered. A failed launch costs a full spec-check pass plus a relaunch. Proposed: resume the spec check's session once with the shape error and the expected formats (Ready, or Question blocks) before the retry from scratch; and say in the launch output which item failed and that rerunning is safe. Related: S243, S116, S258, S264. Absorbed from S300 (retired into this row 2026-11-07): Wave 8, 2026-11-05 (friction F44): the read-only spec check for S278 ran rg ... | head -20, the sandbox denied it, and ork failed the whole spec check ('spec check failed: spec-check exited ok: permission denied: Bash: rg -n ... | head -20'); the wave did not start; a plain relaunch passed. One occurrence so far. Code (read 2026-11-07 at a1114e2): the retry loop is RunSpecCheck's (internal/engine/speccheck.go:144-156); it reruns runSpecCheckOnce from scratch once, only after a shape error, a moved main or a changed status; any denial returns at once (speccheck.go:281-282), pinned by TestSpecCheckStopsOnPermissionDenials (internal/engine/speccheck_test.go:180); the spec check never resumes a session (no Resume in speccheck.go). Needed, in this same loop: a round that ended with denied read commands or a report-shape failure is resumed once in the SAME session with a nudge that names the denials or the shape error and the expected forms, instead of failing or starting over; a second failure fails the check as today, and the launch output names the item and says a rerun is safe. Re-check before building the denial half: S277's Done when (internal/engine/brief.go:153-167) gives a read-only role only 'You may only read the tree' and no command-form rule; the 'one command per call, no pipe' lines (brief.go:161-165, commit 7bb435b) are for a Grok read-only role only. note_records.text: **2026-11-08** — Later (S307): an unreadable or newer vendors-out.json is reported only in the daemon log (the auto-started daemon's stderr goes to a log file): surface it as a status/footer warning or an ork doctor finding. ork vendor and the footer cannot tell an owner mark from an automatic mark that reads the same. Owner choices made by the implementer, unconfirmed: file name vendors-out.json, --until formats HH:MM / YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM / RFC 3339, a failed store write refuses the mark with an internal error.

fields.findings: Waves 7-8, 2026-11-05 (friction F43): the owner's ork vendor out grok mark was lost three times, once by a daemon restart and twice silently when the daemon idled out (daemon_idle_minutes effective 10) while a wave start was held on a spec question waiting for the owner. The next run put Grok on the reviewer row and stopped (reviewer round 1 exited unclassified), costing a full implementer round (about 28 min) each time. Fact: an owner mark has no expiry (internal/daemon/vendors.go:30-31) but lives only in daemon memory; ork vendor list after the idle exit printed 'no vendor is out'. Needed: owner marks (ork vendor out) are written to ork's state directory and reloaded at daemon start, so they end only with ork vendor back; automatic rate-limit and credit marks keep their own expiry (S273). The help text 'a restart clears them' changes to match. Related: S273, S169, S182. Absorbed from S273 (retired into this row 2026-11-07): Owner 2026-11-03: the codex weekly limit message said it resets 7:12 AM on 4 Nov, but ork vendor out takes no end time, so the mark lasts until ork vendor back (or, today, a daemon restart). Still needed, as part of this row: (a) ork vendor out VENDOR --until TIME sets an owner mark that ends at TIME, is persisted with the other owner marks, and is shown with its end time in the footer and ork vendor list; (b) reading a reset time from the vendor's own message is done only once a real captured message with a reset time exists as a test fixture; until then automatic marks keep their fixed expiry (MarkOut sets Until to at plus VendorOutFor, internal/engine/vendors.go:162; owner marks have none, MarkOutOwner at internal/engine/vendors.go:172-182). Do not write a parser against a guessed message shape.

items.title: Self-host daemon rebuilds itself: drain, build, swap, restart
items.short_title: Daemon auto-rebuild

note_records.text:
**2026-11-18** — Human checks at approval (S431):
- later: With `ork projects set ork --auto-rebuild on`, land a slice that changes internal/engine while another run is implementing; the daemon restarts on the new build after that role ends.

**2026-11-18** — Verified: with auto_rebuild on, a self-host daemon behind main after a landing holds new engine and spec-check role starts, lets running roles finish (none killed), builds through the shared RunBuild helper, checks the new executable (usable and not at the running revision), then ends and starts the successor from the new build. A failed or unchanged build keeps the old daemon, releases the hold and shows 'daemon not rebuilt' with the output; no retry until main moves. Held runs show 'waiting for daemon rebuild' in status, ork status and the TUI. Off by default. go vet, gofmt and go test ./... green (4093 passed, 0 failed); every new assertion mutation-checked. Real-Run test skips only where the temp path is too long for a socket. Human check (land an engine slice with auto_rebuild on) left for the owner; held-run auto-resume is S439.

fields.findings: 2026-11-18: after S332, S403, S405 and S404 landed, the daemon stayed on build 7f5a1f7d, so landed fixes (the changelog-entry gate, ork wait, the tracking commit) did not apply to new runs. `ork daemon restart --rebuild` refuses while any role runs, even with --force (`docs/design.md:3847-3849`, adj 312), and with three runs in flight there was no gap; the orchestrator retried it every 30 s from a shell loop. The rebuild runs in the CLI (`internal/cli/lifecycle.go:88-120`); the daemon only reports behind main (`internal/daemon/build.go:25`, `:173`).

records.title: One clear owner for each relay step; no step lives in two tools
Keep the outer session's context small by moving deterministic work out of it
Use slicer and adjudicate only through their CLIs and JSON output
Follow slicer's relay contract by version, never by copying its text
No unattended runs; the owner attends every relay (open: adj scope.attended)
No tracking state of its own for items, slices, specs, readiness or decisions
No reading or writing .slicer/ or decisions/ files directly
No commits, pushes or merges unless the owner authorizes them for a run
Not an LLM; model work stays in the role agents
One dashboard across projects: roadmaps, decisions and live relays with every agent, stage and progress
Edit and reorder the roadmap from the dashboard, every edit a slicer CLI call
Manage the decision queue from the dashboard, every change an adj CLI call made as the owner
Set up, launch and supervise parallel slice waves across vendors, owner-attended at checkpoints
User experience first: colorful, keyboard-driven TUI with mouse support
Small explicit state: ork owns only its registry, run records and UI preferences
No scheduler: ork does not pick and run waves on its own
One workflow kind for now: the slice relay; no general pipeline language
Deterministic before model: tests, slicer check, fingerprint and report shape checked by ork before any model review
